statement: An admission decision has exactly one implementation, and its blocking set is closed. A condition may block admission only where a ratified rule says it must; every other condition is recorded as a disclosed, non-blocking exception carrying the authority for that classification.

occurrences.defect: The Claim route refused VERIFY_NOT_COMPLETE unless Pulse monitoring AND P&L disclosure were both authorized — a prerequisite the constitution does not have. Marketa's own ratified engine sets REFUSAL_RULE_IDS = {MKT-ADM-003,004,005,006}; Pulse is MKT-ADM-007 and P&L is MKT-ADM-008, both deliberately OUTSIDE it, so their absence evaluates 'missing' and yields NOT_RECOMMENDED, never REFUSED. A panel had invented a gate, and when the authorization table proved absent that self-imposed gate escalated a deploy step into a total block on Claim, Passport and delegation.

canaries.assertion: No file outside the gate constructs `blockingReasons` or decides `eligible` from a blocking code; the blocking and non-blocking vocabularies are disjoint; every non-blocking code carries a cited ratified authority; and with EVERY ancillary signal off (Pulse, P&L, authorization store, partner metadata, diagnostic inconsistencies) Passport is still eligible. Mutation-verified: promoting Pulse to a blocker, and adding a second file that computes `eligible` from a blocking code, each turn the suite red.

notes: Operator instruction, verbatim (2026-08-03): "ONE explicit admission-gate function — do not let every panel invent its own prerequisites. Only genuine constitutional prerequisites may block Passport. Pulse monitoring, P&L disclosure, optional partner metadata, missing ancillary receipts and diagnostic inconsistencies must NOT block Passport unless an existing ratified rule explicitly says they must."

EVIDENCE SEARCH, as instructed and recorded either way: the repo was searched across codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/, docs/, services/ and components/ for a ratified rule making Pulse/P&L a hard admission gate. NONE EXISTS. Four ratified sources say the opposite — Marketa's REFUSAL_RULE_IDS; PRD-GJR-001 §3.7 'transparency is a gateway, never a grant'; §5.8 routing transparency to STANDING eligibility rather than admission; and GJR-VFY-001 §2, that a transparency authorization 'does not prove or create: constitutional authority generally; sponsorship; bounded delegation; payment authority; FS Runtime admission; Standing.'

The non-blocking classifications are carried as DATA (`NON_BLOCKING_EVIDENCE`), not comments, so a surface can show the operator why a red-looking condition is not stopping them, and so a future agent proposing to promote one to a blocker must first contradict a named source.

A canary in this set was CORRECTED during implementation with its reason recorded: the first version flagged any file containing a blocking-code string and caught Marketa's evidence layer, which pushes 'control-proof-stale' onto an `unresolvedClaims` list. That is an OBSERVATION, not a decision. Detecting the decision signature instead preserved the canary rather than weakening it to pass.
